name: Paginated Users API
desc:
You are writing the extraction step of a pipeline that copies users from a partner's REST API. The HTTP layer is already written: you receive a function fetch_page that performs the call and returns the raw response body.

def fetch_page(cursor: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Calls GET /users?cursor=<cursor> and returns the raw response body (a JSON string).
    Use cursor=None for the first page. Raises an exception if the cursor is invalid."""

Each response body has this shape:

{"data": [ <user>, <user>, ... ], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "c2"}

A user object looks like this. Any field may be missing or null, at any level, and unknown fields may be present:

{
  "id": 1,
  "email": " Amina@Mail.COM ",
  "profile": {"first_name": "Amina", "last_name": "Benali"},
  "address": {"city": "Casablanca", "country_code": "ma", "geo": {"lat": 33.57, "lng": -7.59}},
  "tags": ["vip", "beta"]
}

Pagination rules

  1. The first call is fetch_page(None).
  2. While the current page has has_more equal to true, fetch the next page with fetch_page(next_cursor). A page may have an empty data list while has_more is still true.
  3. Stop as soon as a page has has_more equal to false, even if its next_cursor is not null. Do not call fetch_page more times than needed.

Output

Return a list of dicts, one per user, in the order in which the API returned them. Users whose id is missing or null are skipped. Each dict has exactly these keys:

key type rule
user_id str id converted to str (id can be an int or a str; 0 is a valid id)
email str or None stripped and lowercased; None if missing or null
full_name str or None profile.first_name and profile.last_name, each stripped, joined with a single space; a part that is missing, null or blank is skipped; None if no part is left
city str or None address.city as is; None if missing or null
country str or None address.country_code stripped and uppercased; None if missing, null or blank
lat float or None address.geo.lat as a float; None if missing or null
lng float or None address.geo.lng as a float; None if missing or null
n_tags int number of elements of tags; 0 if missing or null

Example

Pages returned by the API:

fetch_page(None) == '{"data": [{"id": 1, "email": " Amina@Mail.COM ", "profile": {"first_name": "Amina", "last_name": "Benali"}, "address": {"city": "Casablanca", "country_code": "ma", "geo": {"lat": 33.57, "lng": -7.59}}, "tags": ["vip", "beta"]}, {"id": "u-2", "email": null, "profile": {"first_name": "Omar"}, "address": null}], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "c2"}'
fetch_page("c2") == '{"data": [{"id": 3, "profile": {"first_name": " ", "last_name": "Idrissi"}, "address": {"city": "Rabat", "geo": null}, "tags": []}], "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null}'

Expected return value:

[
    {"user_id": "1", "email": "amina@mail.com", "full_name": "Amina Benali", "city": "Casablanca",
     "country": "MA", "lat": 33.57, "lng": -7.59, "n_tags": 2},
    {"user_id": "u-2", "email": None, "full_name": "Omar", "city": None,
     "country": None, "lat": None, "lng": None, "n_tags": 0},
    {"user_id": "3", "email": None, "full_name": "Idrissi", "city": "Rabat",
     "country": None, "lat": None, "lng": None, "n_tags": 0},
]

Function signature

def ingest_users(fetch_page) -> list:
    ...

Constraints

  • Python 3 standard library only (json is available). No network access: only call fetch_page.
  • Up to 10^4 pages, up to 100 users per page.

The functions described in the task (the API) are provided by the tests: you only write your function.

[execution time limit] 4 seconds (py3)
[memory limit] 1 GB
howto:
Où écrire
  1. Écris dans l'éditeur à droite, fichier solution.py.
  2. Complète la fonction ingest_users(fetch_page). Garde son nom et ses paramètres : ce sont les tests qui l'appellent, avec leurs propres données. N'écris pas d'appel à la fonction toi-même.
  3. Les fonctions décrites dans l'énoncé (l'API) sont fournies par les tests, qui les passent à ta fonction : tu écris seulement ta fonction et tu les appelles.
Ce que tu dois renvoyer
  1. Ta fonction doit renvoyer le résultat avec return. Un print ne compte pas : il sort seulement dans l'onglet Console Output.
  2. Dans les résultats des tests, result est ce que ta fonction a renvoyé, et calls la liste des appels qu'elle a faits à l'API. Les deux doivent être identiques à « Expected return value » : un appel en trop ou dans le mauvais ordre suffit pour que le test soit faux.
Lancer et vérifier
  1. Clique RUN TESTS (ou Ctrl + Entrée) : ton test visible tourne.
  2. Quand c'est bon, tu vois en vert « Tests passed: 1/1. ». Sinon, ouvre le test marqué Wrong answer : compare « Expected return value » et « Your return value », et clique VIEW DIFF pour colorer les cases différentes. Runtime error veut dire que ton code a planté : le message est dans le test.
  3. Clique SUBMIT : ta note sur 100 compte aussi 4 tests cachés. Soumets dès que quelques tests passent, puis améliore et resoumets : c'est la dernière soumission qui compte.
